items.title: 61520_Teddy Edwards oral history interview
items.q: I think it was Artie Shaw, and 'The Blue Flame' was his theme song during that time.

ctx.x: And then they had the Blue Flame, which was run by a very popular guy around home named Joe Ketchum(?). Now, that was... He named it after Woody Herman's theme song, "Blue Flame," when Woody first came out... Was it Herman or Shaw? Which one was "Blue Flame"? I think it was Artie Shaw, and "The Blue Flame" was his theme song during that time. Anyway, it was one of the clarinet players. And he named this place after that. And it was a really nice place, you know, really nice, but it was still over there in all…

There was a fellow who used to come through.... I've got to mention this fellow, because I wrote a song about him, and I recorded it on my album that I made, Feelings, on Muse Records. They used to call him Bear Tracks. And he would go around with these overalls on, and he'd be barefooted all the time. And he'd walk up through this mud, you know, and you could see where he's been because he's barefoot -- everybody called him "Bear Tracks," you know. And he'd go from place to place. And the minute that you'd take…
